Equip: ranged damaged increased by 20% when health goes below 20%

content.text:
Absolutely. The gear is already moving in the right direction with proc packages, ammo affinities, kill chains, crit interactions, and conditional effects. I’d lean harder into “this changes how I play” items:

- **Bloodletter’s Band** — Equip: ranged attacks deal 30% more damage to targets below 50% health.
- **Gravewind Cloak** — Equip: moving after killing an enemy makes you invisible for 1 turn.
- **Bracers of Reversal** — Equip: when you dodge, your next attack cannot miss and deals 2× damage.
- **Marauder’s Harness** — Equip: melee kills restore 25% stamina; ranged kills restore 10% stamina.
- **Cinderwake Boots** — Equip: moving through fire leaves a burning tile behind you.
- **The Last Stand** — Equip: while below 20% health, gain 50% damage reduction but cannot retreat.
- **Deadeye Loop** — Equip: every third ranged hit pierces the target and the enemy behind it.
- **Gambler’s Mantle** — Equip: critical hits deal 3× damage; normal hits deal 15% less.
- **Witch-King’s Circlet** — Equip: damaging an enemy with a spell marks it; your next weapon hit detonates the mark.
- **Trollhide Belt** — Equip: recover 2% max health whenever you end a turn without attacking.
- **Stormcaller Gloves** — Equip: thrown weapons have a 20% chance to bounce to a nearby enemy.
- **Ashen Oath** — Equip: fire damage increases as your health decreases, up to 100% more damage.

The strongest design space seems to be:

1. threshold effects — health, stamina, mana, enemy count;
2. rhythm effects — every third hit, alternating attacks, after moving;
3. conversion effects — crits into lightning, stamina into damage, kills into defense;
4. commitment effects — powerful bonuses paired with an actual restriction.

I’d make the next batch mostly belts, gloves, boots, and rings, with each item having one memorable rule instead of stacking five ordinary bonuses.
BRO!!! these are nasty--- I love it

YES. That’s exactly the lane: gear that makes you invent a build around it.

My immediate “must-add” tier:

- **Bracers of Reversal** — dodge → guaranteed 2× counterattack.
- **Deadeye Loop** — every third ranged hit pierces.
- **Cinderwake Boots** — movement leaves fire behind.
- **Witch-King’s Circlet** — spell mark → weapon detonation.
- **Gambler’s Mantle** — huge crits, weaker normal hits.

Those feel like items players will remember finding.
these are fucking awesome -- make em!

I’m using the item-authoring workflow plus JSHack’s inspection tools. I’ll implement the five standout items we just picked—Reversal, Deadeye Loop, Cinderwake, Witch-King’s Circlet, and Gambler’s Mantle—by extending the existing proc/equipment surfaces, then prove each mechanic with focused tests.

content.text:
Fixed.

The gear is now split into its canonical files:

- `gloves.js` — Bracers of Reversal
- `rings.js` — Deadeye Loop
- `boots.js` — Cinderwake Boots
- `helms.js` — Witch-King’s Circlet
- `armors.js` — Gambler’s Mantle

I also added **Call the Brood** to Witch-King’s Circlet:

> Use: summon three loyal spiders. 200-turn cooldown.

The standalone `specialGear.js` is gone, and content/catalog tests pass.
Don't forget about "Use:" -- that might be fun.

Absolutely. Passive procs make gear memorable; `Use:` abilities make it feel like you’re carrying a weaponized decision.

Good pairings:

- Bracers of Reversal — Use: enter a perfect counter stance for 5 turns.
- Deadeye Loop — Use: mark one enemy; your next ranged hit pierces every target in its line.
- Cinderwake Boots — Use: ignite a ring of fire around you.
- Witch-King’s Circlet — Use: summon three loyal spiders, 200-turn cooldown.
- Gambler’s Mantle — Use: double your next hit’s damage—or make it deal nothing.

That’s definitely a design axis worth using aggressively.
I wouldn't keep adding to the gear we just made, I'd make more

Exactly. Keep the current five focused, then make a separate batch where the identity is the active ability.

- **Widowmaker’s Brooch** — ring, rare  
  `Use: summon three loyal cave spiders. 200-turn cooldown.`

- **Lantern of the Lost Hunt** — neck, uncommon  
  `Use: reveal every hostile creature on the floor for 20 turns. 40-turn cooldown.`

- **Gravemarch Greaves** — boots, epic  
  `Use: teleport to the tile you stood on three turns ago. 60-turn cooldown.`

- **The Red Button** — belt, rare  
  `Use: sacrifice 25% current health to reset your equipped weapon’s cooldowns.`

- **Crown of Borrowed Faces** — helm, legendary  
  `Use: disguise yourself as a nearby enemy for 30 turns. Attacking breaks the disguise.`

That gives us a whole new family of “I found this and immediately changed my plan” gear without muddying the passives we just made.
these are all sick - love em ;-)
Hell yes. That’s the next gear family: active, weird, build-defining toys with cooldowns and consequences.
these are cool -- we could blend shit too -- ;-)

Oh absolutely. The best ones can have a passive that sets up the `Use:` ability:

- **Widowmaker’s Brooch** — passive: ranged hits mark prey; `Use:` summon three spiders, and each spider hunts a marked target.
- **Gravemarch Greaves** — passive: leaving fire behind; `Use:` teleport backward and ignite both departure and arrival tiles.
- **The Red Button** — passive: damage increases as HP falls; `Use:` sacrifice health to instantly refresh abilities.
- **Crown of Borrowed Faces** — passive: bonus damage while disguised; `Use:` copy a nearby enemy’s appearance.
- **Lantern of the Lost Hunt** — passive: revealed enemies take extra damage; `Use:` reveal the floor and mark every hostile.

That blend gives each item a passive identity plus a deliberate “oh shit” button.
love it -- make it so!

I’m adding a separate active-gear family, keeping the original five untouched. I’ll give each new item a slot/rarity, a passive proc where it fits, and a real `Use:` ability with cooldowns/consequences, split into the canonical item files.
